note: Corps of Engineers campground below Elk City Dam on the Elk River, about 5 miles northwest of Independence and below Table Mound's rock formations. Gravel back-in sites in two loops: the electric sites on the north loop and along its east side, non-electric at the north end and on a small south loop; the wooded east side runs along the river. Group shelter, basketball and sand volleyball; beside the Elk River Hiking Trail and the mountain-bike trails. --Claude
summary: rec.gov API (2026-11-06): 14 back-in gravel sites, 7 with 50 A + water ($16), 7 non-electric ($10), shelter $30, 14 nights per rolling 30, vault toilets + dump station; calendar open through winter. All groups re-sourced manual; max_stay 14, platform, facilities added. Waterfront lead: not waterfront -> riverview (rec.gov tags the non-electric sites Riverfront). Phone/website/pin confirmed.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (contrary claim): stored 'not waterfront'; recreation.gov tags the 7 non-electric sites (1-4, 9-11) 'Proximity to Water: Riverfront'. Imagery (leaf-off): the Elk River channel is ~35-45 m wide along the east side (river, not creek). Sites 6-9 on the east side of the north loop sit ~25-35 m from the water across an unbroken wooded strip, no road or day use between; south-loop sites 1-4 are ~50 m back through woods. Open bank between site and water is not there, so riverfront is not earned; a filtered river view through the tree belt is. Propose 'riverview'; if you'd rather not move it on a leaf-off look, keep 'not waterfront'.
